newsitem.title: USA: Florida judge threatened workers: testimony.
newsitem.headline: Florida judge threatened workers: testimony.

text.p: A Florida judge on trial for allegedly bizarre, overbearing behaviour threatened to send two court staff members to jail because she did not like their work, the employees told a special panel Wednesday.
One also testified that Judge Gail Graziano bullied her into hiring Graziano's longtime companion, Ethel Rosa, for a job the woman was not qualified to perform.
Graziano faces additional charges of threatening a law clerk with a pistol and charging into another judge's courtroom during a murder case to berate a stenographer for parking in the wrong space.

At stake is whether the judge of 13 years will be removed from the bench. The trial is being heard before the Florida Judicial Qualifications Commission, which will forward a recommendation to the state Supreme Court.

Evelyn Bible, a court employee who manages jury pools, testified that one day she found herself with fewer potential jurors than Graziano wanted. "She said 'I want what I want or you're going to jail'," Bible said.

In another incident, Tony Landry, a computer technician, said he sent a memo to a county administrator explaining how to save money on a software purchase Graziano had approved. In a meeting with Landry present, Graziano raised the memo with his supervisor, he said.
"She said, 'If Mr. Landry does something like that again he'll find himself in jail,'" he said, adding: "She wasn't smiling."
Special prosecuting counsel John Jopling has accused Graziano of "surrendering to the arrogance of power."
Ellis Rubin, a Miami attorney defending the 45-year-old judge, said she was a strong feminist who challenged the sexist and racist practices of her judicial circuit.
Public hearings on judicial complaints are rare in Florida. More often both sides reach some agreement before complaints reach the trial stage.
Graziano, from the beginning, demanded a public trial. Some 28 witnessses are scheduled to testify against her.
